newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds pressured by dollar, talk of variable repos.
newsitem.headline: Bunds pressured by dollar, talk of variable repos.

text.p: German debt prices continued to fall in early trade on Tuesday as the weakness of the mark unsettled investors and amid mild speculation that the Bundesbank may switch to a variable-rate repo tender either before or after its upcoming four-week summer break.
September Bund futures were quoted down 25 basis points at 102.42 at 0706 GMT after falling as low as 102.32 earlier in the session.
Dealers said the contract had technical support at 102.17. One dealer said the current fall could take September Bunds down to 101.90, followed by a rebound.

Several dealers said the market was contemplating the possibility that the Bundesbank may return to variable-rate tenders for securities repurchase agreements. Repo tenders have been fixed at a rate of 3.00 percent since August 1996.

In variable-rate tenders, the repo rate is determined by banks' bids for repos rather than being fixed directly by the Bundesbank. Dealers said a switch to variable-rate repos could prompt banks to bid the repo rate above three percent.
One dealer said that the market was also looking at the possibility the Bundesbank may raise its repo rate after the summer break while sticking to fixed rates.
"People aren't really talking about it yet but they are thinking that one of those two things may happen," one Frankfurt-based dealer said.
The rationale behind a repo rate rise would be to stem the mark's depreciation on currency markets and to prevent any rise in consumer inflation which may result from the increase in import prices.
But Armin Kayser, bond market analyst at Swiss Bank Corporation in Frankfurt, said he could not imagine an early return to variable-rate repo tenders.
"We've already had a strong rise in import prices but little evidence of imported inflation in consumer prices," Kayser said.

"Consumer demand is weak and it would be perverse to raise rates at a time of record unemployment. My feeling is that the Bundesbank can wait a few months to see how import prices are impacting consumer inflation."
Dealers said they will pay attention to U.S. June retail sales which are due to be released at 1230 GMT.
